method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, to the design decided for Michael (D1-D8 in NOTES.md) and the defaults ruled on 2026-10-18: a seat-neutral core (gva-core.l4, ten regulative rules) and one seat layer for three seats (gva-seat.l4), the seat a parameter that every exported question takes first, and (D8) the situation a parameter too: within a role, a question that arises only in a situation takes that situation's fact straight after the role and answers `does not arise for you` without reading any other input when it does not hold, the questions of one situation sharing one input with the same name, type and @desc; each regulative rule projected into does it apply, by when, have I complied (the rule run over the events inside the question with CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED, with acts dated before a rule's start settled from the dates) and what follows; no exported question takes a DEONTIC or EVENT input; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. An independent verification pass (gva-ver, 2026-10-25) found 3 major and 6 minor issues; the fix pass (gva-fix, 2026-10-25) is recorded in NOTES.md fixes 15-24, and the situations pass (gva-sit, 2026-10-25) under D8 and points 25-33. No pipeline, no coverage table, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Compilation of the Graffiti Vandalism Act 2016 (No. 16 of 2016; Pt 1 from 11 Jul 2016, the rest from 12 Oct 2016), including the Local Government Legislation Amendment Act 2016 (No. 26 of 2016) Pt 3 Div 14 (from 21 Jan 2017); law_a147110, mrdoc 29645, retrieved 2026-09-07 from legislation.wa.gov.au, deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_29645.txt. Encoded as far as the Act's periods need them (gva-dates.l4): Interpretation Act 1984 s 61(1)(b), (e), (2) and the Public and Bank Holidays Act 1972 s 5 and Second Schedule, apart from the days appointed by proclamation. Read, cited and not encoded: Sentencing Act 1995 s 9, Interpretation Act 1984 ss 64, 71, State Administrative Tribunal Act 2004 s 92, The Criminal Code s 731 and Local Government Act 1995 s 1.4, all deposited under subjects/au/wa/.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run gva-dates.l4 ; l4 run gva-core.l4 ; l4 run gva-seat.l4 ; l4 run gva-cases-core.l4 ; l4 run gva-cases-seat.l4 ; l4 check gva-seat.l4
checks.result: 474 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in all five files (175 core + 299 seat, 2026-10-25, after the gva-sit pass); 22 #TRACEs in gva-cases-core.l4 with an expect line, each read and as expected (12 breaches, 5 rules still waiting, 3 permissions lapsed without a breach, 2 fulfilled after the lapse); l4 check gva-seat.l4: Check succeeded; a script listing every @export's inputs, types and @desc: 38 questions, each takes `my role` IS A Role first, each of the six situation inputs is identical in name, type and @desc wherever taken and comes straight after the role (the notice after consent, the objection after the notice), each role branch reads its situation input first, none takes a DEONTIC or EVENT input; the 299 seat cases are 7 helper cases, 76 cases for the two other roles, 51 cases for each situation value that does not hold (later inputs ASSUMEd) and 165 in the situation that holds; negative controls on scratch copies (s 61(1)(e) off, the s 23 written-notice date ignored, the s 12 owner fact ignored; and for D8, a read moved before each kind of situation check) each caught
checks.consider_evaltrace: On 1.6.98 CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED works and OTHERWISE accepts a breached trace, but WHEN BREACH is a parse error and OTHERWISE cannot tell a breach from a pending rule; the seat helper therefore runs the rule over the act done, or over the act done now when it has not been, and so tells done in time, not done in time and still open apart correctly (NOTES.md finding 20). Where the rule cannot tell (an act dated before the rule starts, finding 23) the questions settle it from the dates first, as design D5's fallback says.
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.
checks.assumed_inputs: On 1.6.98 reading an ASSUMEd BOOLEAN, NUMBER or DATE, or CONSIDERing an ASSUMEd value with no OTHERWISE, fails the assertion, but a CONSIDER with OTHERWISE quietly takes OTHERWISE (NOTES.md finding 31). The seat's helpers over the notice and the accusation therefore list every value; the core's OTHERWISE reads of how the mark was applied, the kind of item and the thing forfeited are covered by the script's check that the role and situation are read first.

scope: In: ss 3, 4 (adult, child, graffiti implement, offender, possession), 5, 6, 7 (with the s 7(2) defence), 8, 10, 12 (the owner only, with owner asked as a fact), 13, 14 (public place, as a gloss), 18(1)-(5), 19(3)-(7), 20, 21, 22(1)-(2), 23, 24(1), (3), 25, 27, 28, 29 (the warrant as an input), 30. Out: ss 1, 2, 9, 11, 15-17, 22(3), 26 (noted), 31, 32, 33-44. Judgments are inputs answered conditionally. The last day to object (s 22(2)) or apply for review (s 23(3)) is moved off a Saturday, Sunday or Second Schedule public holiday under the Interpretation Act s 61(1)(e); the King's Birthday and other proclaimed, public service and local holidays are not counted, and the time a s 18 notice sets is not moved.

regulative_rules: s 5(1) -- a person must not damage another person's property by graffiti without consent
s 6(1) -- a person must not possess a thing with the intention of applying graffiti with it
s 7 -- a person must not sell a graffiti implement to a child, unless they believed on reasonable grounds the buyer was an adult
s 18(2), (5) -- the notice recipient must ensure the graffiti is obliterated within the time in the notice
s 19(3) -- the local government may obliterate the graffiti
s 22(2) -- the affected person may object within 28 days after the notice is given, or any further time allowed
s 23(3) -- the affected person may apply for review within 42 days after the right to apply arose
s 24(1) -- the notice is suspended until the objection or application is decided
s 25(1) -- the local government may obliterate graffiti applied without consent
ss 27, 28 -- the local government may enter only with consent, a warrant, or at least 24 hours' notice
